It is caused by a deficiency of the hexosaminidase A (HEX A) enzyme, which is necessary for breaking down GM2-ganglioside within cells; the disease occurs when harmful quantities of gangliosides accumulate in the nerve cells of the brain, leading to progressive neurological damage

The disorder is inherited when an individual receives two variant copies of the HEXA gene — one from each parent — and the specific type of Tay-Sachs (infantile, juvenile late-onset) is determined by the degree of residual HEX A enzyme activity and the age at which symptoms first appear
